title: Nazara Technologies preferential issue: Q2 FY27 report
description: Nazara Technologies preferential issue update: CARE Ratings' Q2 FY27 report shows ₹395.61 crore used for expansion, plus a ₹1.30 crore AIF investment.

body.text: The Nazara Technologies preferential issue is back in focus after the company filed its Monitoring Agency Report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. According to Investywise, the report, issued by CARE Ratings Limited, shows how the money raised is being spent, including a small AIF investment and a spending overshoot that the Board has since ratified. For anyone tracking how Indian gaming companies deploy fresh capital, it is a useful look at the paperwork behind the headlines.
What the Nazara Technologies preferential issue report covers
The report is required under SEBI regulations. Its job is to give shareholders an independent view of whether money raised through a preferential issue is going where the company said it would.

Investywise says the key findings are an investment in an Alternative Investment Fund that the original offer document did not explicitly detail, and a reallocation of funds towards expansion and growth.
During the second quarter of fiscal year 2027, the report records ₹1.30 crore going into the Lumikai Fund II India Advantage Scheme, an AIF. The company classed this under "Expansion and Growth".

The monitoring agency flagged one point: putting issue proceeds into an AIF was not specifically described in the offer document. The amount is small, but the disclosure matters because it concerns how closely spending follows what was promised to investors.
Expansion spending went past the revised allocation
The bigger number sits under Expansion and Growth. The revised allocation for this object is ₹355.50 crore, but the company reported utilization of ₹395.61 crore in Q2 FY27.

items: Excess over revised allocation: ₹40.11 crore, or 11.28%
Board ratification: a resolution dated November 6, 2026
Funding source for the gap: funds reallocated from "General Corporate Purposes" to "Expansion and Growth"

body.text: As of September 30, 2026, only ₹0.13 crore of the funds received remained unutilized. Another ₹78.00 crore was still receivable from one investor, according to the report as summarized by Investywise.
Other points noted in the report

The report also refers to Nazara's standalone net loss of ₹934.97 crore in FY26, which Investywise says was primarily due to an impairment loss. It further notes changes in Key Managerial Personnel and a high percentage of pledged promoter shares. The source does not give details on who changed roles or how large the pledge is, so those points remain open.

Watch how the remaining ₹78.00 crore receivable from the investor is settled, and whether later monitoring reports show further reallocation between objects. Any clarification on the AIF investment or the KMP changes would also be worth following. Since the Board ratified the excess only on November 6, the next quarterly report should show how these decisions play out.

faqs.q: What is the Nazara Technologies monitoring agency report for Q2 FY27?
faqs.a: It is a SEBI-mandated report, issued by CARE Ratings Limited for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, on how Nazara is using the proceeds of its preferential issue, according to Investywise.

faqs.q: How much did Nazara invest in the Lumikai AIF?
faqs.a: The report records an investment of ₹1.30 crore in the Lumikai Fund II India Advantage Scheme during Q2 FY27. It was classed under Expansion and Growth, though the offer document did not specifically mention deploying proceeds into an AIF.

faqs.q: Did Nazara overspend its revised allocation for expansion and growth?
faqs.a: Yes. Utilization was ₹395.61 crore against a revised allocation of ₹355.50 crore, an excess of ₹40.11 crore or 11.28%. The Board ratified it through a resolution dated November 6, 2026.
